title: Air-Fried Totopos: A Novel Snack Evaluated by Microscopy Techniques for Optimal Food Qualities
content: Air frying is an emerging cooking method based on the rapid circulation of hot air by forced convection around the food uniformly to obtain a food product similar to oil frying. The main idea of air frying is to reduce the amount of oil used in the conventional fried technique [1]. This technology was patented by TurboChef Technologies in 2005. However, its popularity and demand in the market have recently been gaining popularity as a healthier alternative to traditional frying. Currently, air frying has been studied in most popular foods such as nuggets, French fries, fish, vegetables, and meat since the reduction of oil is around 80% and the acrylamide content is reduced drastically [1,2]. However, the physical properties have not been entirely studied, especially the texture and microstructure of the food. In this sense, the present research focuses on the study of the microstructure and texture properties of air-fried tortilla chips named “totopos”, a popular food from Mexico with enhanced food quality properties.
